question.problem:
Given that 

$$
{∮}_{C}(x+y)\,dx-{x}^{2}y\,dy={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,{\int }_{0}^{5}\boxed{}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $C$ is the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=25$ oriented counterclockwise, what is the missing part of the equation?
question.worked_solution:
Green's theorem states that 

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, the region $D$ and its boundary $C$ satisfy the conditions of Green's theorem:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223987/assets/0470588a034222b183694b087d417e8ead0d2fd72357e796373794d00523708f.png)

Since $P(x,y)=x+y$ and $Q(x,y)=-{x}^{2}y,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=1,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=-2xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(x+y)\,dx-{x}^{2}y\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2xy-1)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the region $D$ can be represented in polar coordinates as

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 5,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi \}.
$$

The change of variables formula for plane polar coordinates states that 

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

Therefore, we can write our double integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}(-2xy-1)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}(-2\cdot r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -1)\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={∬}_{Δ}(-2{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -r)\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,{\int }_{0}^{5}-{r}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )-r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
